summary.text: Jennifer Todd is the Democratic nominee for Illinois's 15th Congressional District and a nurse and small business owner from Edwardsville. She won a four-way Democratic primary in March 2026 and is making her first run for office, against incumbent Republican Mary Miller.

paragraphs.text: Todd was born in Illinois and graduated from Centralia High School.
She earned an associate degree from Kaskaskia Community College and bachelor's degrees from Southern Illinois University Edwardsville and Southern Illinois University Carbondale.

Her career experience includes working as a nurse and small business owner; NPR Illinois / St. Louis Public Radio describes her as an Edwardsville nurse, and in her WTTW voter guide entry she lists her occupation as retired registered nurse and reports no previous political experience.
Todd won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 45.7% of the vote over Paul Davis, Randy Raley and Kyle Nudo.
In the primary she presented herself as someone who understands working-class struggles, having used Medicaid, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and unemployment benefits.
She lives in Edwardsville, less than a mile outside the district, and told the outlet she would move to Logan County if elected.

sources.title: Democrat wants to unseat a 3-term Republican in ultra-conservative Illinois district
sources.publisher: NPR Illinois / St. Louis Public Radio
